AIClassifierSelection.title: AIClassifierSelection

items.description: An 'engine:model' pair; the split is on the first colon.

AIConfigRequirements.description:
What every completions route must offer, checked at build.

Attributes:
    capabilities: Capability names each route's primary must support,
        without the `supports_` prefix (structured_output, tool_use,
        streaming, async, batch, token_counting, ...).
    second_provider: True requires each route to hold a model on a
        provider other than its primary's.
    mode: "warn" logs an unmet requirement; "strict" raises.
AIConfigRequirements.title: AIConfigRequirements

AIFallbackCandidate.description:
One (engine, model) pair in a fallback chain.

Attributes:
    engine: Completions engine token, as the factory accepts it.
    model: Model name for that engine; blank means the engine default.
    base_url: Optional API base-URL override for engines that accept one.
AIFallbackCandidate.title: AIFallbackCandidate

AIFallbackCooldownPolicy.description:
How long a failed candidate rests.

Attributes:
    enabled: False turns cooldowns off; every call starts at the primary.
    seconds: Rest per reason value (for example {"rate_limited": 10}),
        merged over DICT_DEFAULT_COOLDOWN_SECONDS. 0 means no rest.
AIFallbackCooldownPolicy.title: AIFallbackCooldownPolicy

AIRouterClassifierConfig.description:
Which classifier the router uses.

Attributes:
    engine: Classification engine token, or "none" to route without a
        classifier. None means the factory's own resolution
        (CLASSIFIER_ENGINE, then openai-decisions when OPENAI_API_KEY is set).
    model: Classification model; None means the engine's default.
    base_url: Optional API base-URL override.
    timeout_seconds: Per-call classifier timeout.
    instructions: Prose prepended to the built-in routing instructions.
    min_confidence: When the classifier reports a confidence below this
        (0 to 1), the request goes one tier above the classifier's pick.
        None turns the check off; a classifier that reports no
        confidence keeps its pick.
AIRouterClassifierConfig.title: AIRouterClassifierConfig

AIRouterConfig.description:
The router's tiers and policy.

Attributes:
    tiers: Ascending capability; at least one.
    classifier: Classifier selection; None means the factory's resolution.
    default_tier: Tier used when classification is unavailable; None
        means the default chain (the configured completions LLM).
    on_exhausted: When a tier's chain is exhausted on a trigger reason,
        "escalate" tries the next tier up; "any" tries every tier above
        the pick, then the tiers below it, nearest first; "raise"
        re-raises.
    followup: How a follow-up turn of a plain conversation (one with an
        earlier assistant turn and no tool calls) is routed.
        "reclassify" classifies each turn on its own; "ratchet" never
        routes it below the tier that served this client's previous
        call. One client per conversation makes the ratchet exact; a
        client shared across conversations should pass the floor per
        call as provider_options["route_floor"] instead.
    fallback_on: Default trigger reasons for every tier's chain; None
        means the factory's resolution (COMPLETIONS_FALLBACK_ON, then the
        library default).
AIRouterConfig.title: AIRouterConfig

AIRouterTier.description:
One complexity tier.

Attributes:
    name: Lowercase token, unique in the config; the classifier returns it.
    description: Prose the classifier reads to recognize the tier. Built
        in for easy, medium, and hard; required otherwise.
    candidates: The tier's models in order: the primary, then its chain.
    fallback_on: Reasons that move a request along the tier's chain;
        None means the router-level default.
    thinking: The tier's thinking level (off, minimal, low, medium,
        high, max); None means the router's level. A per-call level
        still wins.

models.description: The tier's models in order, the primary first: 'engine:model' strings (comma-separated pairs allowed) or {engine, model, base_url} objects. Same as candidates.

AIRouterTier.title: AIRouterTier

AIThinkingLevel.description:
How much a model should think before answering, provider-neutral.

Members, in order:
    OFF: No thinking. Models whose thinking is always on apply their
        lowest level instead and record it.
    MINIMAL: The least thinking a model offers above off.
    LOW: Light reasoning; quick answers.
    MEDIUM: The default. Balanced depth, mapped to each provider's own
        medium (Anthropic `effort: medium`, OpenAI `reasoning_effort:
        medium`, Gemini `thinking_level: medium`).
    HIGH: Deep reasoning.
    MAX: The most a model offers.
AIThinkingLevel.title: AIThinkingLevel

AiFallbackReason.description:
Why a failed provider request is a candidate for retry on another model.

Set on AiProviderRequestError by each engine from the provider's own error
codes, since an HTTP status alone does not separate a rate limit from an
exhausted quota. Errors that a different model would not fix (validation,
a content refusal) carry no reason. Account-level
failures (a rejected key, a spend cap) do carry one: a candidate on
another provider uses another account.

Members:
    UNAVAILABLE: The provider or model cannot serve right now: 5xx,
        overloaded, model not ready, or the connection failed.
    RATE_LIMITED: A transient 429; the engine's own backoff runs first.
    QUOTA_EXHAUSTED: Billing, credit, quota, or a spend cap is used up,
        so retrying the same model is pointless.
    AUTH_REJECTED: The provider rejected the credentials or the account
        (401/403, an invalid or expired key, a disabled organization).
        Retrying the same provider is pointless; another provider's
        account can still serve.
    TIMEOUT: The caller's own deadline passed before the provider
        answered. Off by default in the fallback layer: the deadline is
        a caller setting, and failing over adds the next candidate's
        wait on top of it. A caller with a short deadline turns it on
        to treat a hung provider as an outage.
    MODEL_UNAVAILABLE: The model id is unknown, retired, or not offered
        in the configured region. Usually a configuration error, so a
        fallback layer should not act on it unless told to.
    INVALID_OUTPUT: The model answered a structured request, and was
        billed for it, but the answer is not valid JSON, not a JSON
        object, or fails the response model. Off by default: a bad
        answer then costs a second billed call on another model, which
        is a spending decision. Turn it on to let the chain try the next
        model and the router escalate on bad output; each discarded
        answer is a wasted line item on the request's cost report.
AiFallbackReason.title: AiFallbackReason

description:
The whole file.

Attributes:
    allow: Model globs the library may use; empty means all.
    deny: Model globs the library may never use; wins over allow.
    completions: Primary engine and model, chain, reasons, retry policy.
    classifier: The classification engine and model.
    router: The complexity router.
    model_check: The configured-model check mode and timeout.
    embeddings, images, videos, voice: Per-capability selections.
    geo_residency: Geo hint (`US`), as AI_API_GEO_RESIDENCY.
    config_version: A label for this configuration (a date, a release,
        a commit); every call the completions client makes carries it
        as the `config_version` tag, next to the computed `config_id`.
